# Jewel Labs

> Hard tech for the diamond trade.

## What we build

An ML automated diamond grading and assorting engine: a desk machine plus the
software and agents that run it. Stones go in the hopper. Cameras and a
spectrometer read each one under known light, a model grades it, and an actuator
drops it in the right bin. Every stone leaves with a record, and the EU customs
filing is built from that record.

The software runs today. The machine is in development. Patent pending on the
full system, the sensing chassis together with the record it writes and the
agents that act on it.

## The sensing heads

- Vision and geometry: machine vision around 360 degrees, a microscope camera for
  inclusions, structured light for the facet map, calibrated LED cycling
  brightfield, darkfield, coaxial and angled.
- Material and weight: a compact spectrometer separates natural from CVD and
  HPHT and exposes treatments, a 365 nm pass reads fluorescence, and a load cell
  takes carat to 0.001 ct on the same stage.
- The heads swap. They sit on one rail against one calibration. Fit the XRF and
  ultrasound pair and the same chassis reads gold and silver instead. The
  software, the agents and the record format are unchanged.

## The chain

The cut plan, the grade and the filing are all built from one record.

1. Cut plan. A rough scan from the scanner already on the factory floor goes to
   the model, which returns where the girdle sits and what comes out of the stone.
2. Read. The polished stone goes in the box and is graded in seconds.
3. Record. One row per stone, permanent, readable by any other system.
4. File. The record is checked against the Kimberley Process certificate and the
   commercial invoice, then filed. If they disagree, the parcel stops on the desk
   instead of at the border.

## Beyond a jewelry stone

The cut planner solves for the end use, not only for a gem. Wafers for thermal
conductivity and semiconductor grade diamond, plates for quantum sensing, cubes
for long term data storage, flake, and classic gems. Only the target shape
changes. About 40 percent of rough carats survive the cut, so every point of
yield is margin.

## Metals

XRF reads composition at the surface and flags plating. Ultrasound reads density
through the core, which is what catches filled and tungsten bars. A load cell
cross checks mass against volume. Same record, same origin papers. If you trade
bullion, get in touch.

## Records

Cut plan, grade, price, filing: rough to export on one record. We are pulling the
commodities onto one rail, and every record is hashed on chain when it is
written, so it can be tokenized.

## Why now

Since 1 January 2026 no natural diamond of 0.5 ct or above enters the EU without
a signed origin statement, and Russian lab grown has been barred since 2024.
Where a stone is cut now sets its US tariff. Rough fell 12 percent in 2025 and
lab grown is down as much as 90 percent, so margin is thin exactly when metals
are near multi year highs.

## The dataset

Every scan stores images, spectra and proportions against the conditions they
were measured under. At volume that is a structured diamond dataset that does not
exist today and cannot be assembled without machines on factory floors. Quantum
sensing and power semiconductors both run on diamond.
